articles.title: OpenAI Releases GPT-5 Turbo with Native Multimodal Reasoning Across Code, Vision, and Audio
articles.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-5 Turbo, featuring deeply integrated multimodal reasoning that can simultaneously process code repositories, visual diagrams, and spoken instructions in a single inference pass. Benchmarks show a 40% improvement on SWE-Bench and ARC-AGI-2 over its predecessor, with significantly reduced hallucination rates. The model also introduces a persistent memory architecture that maintains context across sessions without explicit retrieval augmentation.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves State-of-the-Art on Mathematical Olympiad Problems
articles.summary: DeepMind announced that Gemini Ultra 2 solved 88% of International Mathematical Olympiad 2026 problems at gold-medal level, a significant leap from last year's 72%. The system uses a novel chain-of-verification architecture that self-checks proof steps against formal verification engines in real-time. Researchers noted the approach generalizes well to graduate-level theorem proving, potentially accelerating automated mathematical research.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Begins Commercial Deployment of Figure 03 Humanoid Workers at BMW Plants
articles.summary: Figure Robotics has started deploying its third-generation humanoid robot, Figure 03, across three BMW manufacturing facilities in South Carolina and Bavaria. The robots handle complex sub-assembly tasks including wire harness routing and multi-step quality inspection, operating autonomously for 18-hour shifts. BMW reports a 30% throughput improvement in pilot lines, marking the most significant commercial humanoid deployment to date.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics Atlas Now Performs Dexterous Bi-Manual Manipulation in Unstructured Environments
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics released a major software update for its electric Atlas platform enabling real-time bi-manual dexterous manipulation guided by a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on millions of manipulation demonstrations. The robot can now open packaging, sort mixed recycling, and use common hand tools with human-comparable success rates. The system leverages sim-to-real transfer with less than 10 minutes of real-world fine-tuning per new task.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Constitutional Steering: A New Framework for Fine-Grained AI Behavior Control
articles.summary: Anthropic published a research paper and open-source toolkit for 'Constitutional Steering,' allowing developers to define nuanced behavioral constraints as composable, auditable policy modules rather than monolithic RLHF reward signals. Early adopters report significantly more predictable model behavior in regulated industries like healthcare and finance. The framework includes formal verification hooks that can mathematically prove certain output properties hold under specified input distributions.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm Gate-All-Around Process for Next-Gen AI Accelerators
articles.summary: TSMC announced volume production on its N1.4 process node using gate-all-around nanosheet transistors, with NVIDIA and Broadcom confirmed as lead customers for AI accelerator chips. The node delivers a 35% performance-per-watt improvement over N2, critical for the ballooning power demands of trillion-parameter model training. First commercial chips on the process are expected in data centers by Q1 2027.

articles.title: Meta Releases Llama 4 with 1.5 Trillion MoE Parameters Under Permissive Open License
articles.summary: Meta has open-sourced Llama 4, a 1.5-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that activates roughly 200 billion parameters per forward pass, matching or exceeding GPT-5 on multiple public benchmarks. The release includes full training code, dataset documentation, and distilled variants down to 8B parameters suitable for edge deployment. The open-weight release has reignited debate over the safety implications of frontier-capability models being freely available.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Clearance for Second-Gen Brain-Computer Interface with 16,384 Electrode Channels
articles.summary: The FDA has granted de novo clearance to Neuralink's N2 implant, which quadruples electrode density to 16,384 channels and adds bidirectional stimulation capabilities for both motor and sensory feedback. Clinical trial data from 12 patients showed participants controlling robotic arms with latencies under 50ms and receiving rudimentary tactile feedback. The clearance covers use in patients with cervical spinal cord injuries and ALS, with the first commercial implants scheduled for early 2027.
